note: Guided tours of the sheet (decision 53). target = a [data-tour] mark in the sheet; tab = the sheet tab to open first; optional steps are skipped when their target isn't on screen (e.g. Hostiles outside a GM-run fight); no target = a centred note. Text overlays: i18n/<lang>/tours.json.

steps.title: Your status
steps.text: Name, class and the numbers you check most, always at the top. A value in green or red is changed by a condition (the normal one is shown small beside it).

steps.title: Six tabs
steps.text: Play for the fight, Skills for checks, Gear for money and the market, Dossier for your story and debt, Notes for anything, Progress for XP and talents. When the GM puts a map on the table, a Map tab appears too — with its own short tour.

steps.title: Health & Conditions
steps.text: When you're hit, use Take a hit: type the damage and, for a location attack, where it landed. The sheet takes off your armor, lowers HP and adds the injury or condition. Full heal and Repair armor are here too. Tap a condition to switch it on; Boosts (green) are the good ones the GM may grant.

steps.title: Ready your weapons
steps.text: Pick up to two weapons for your slots: these are what the Attack buttons use. Ammo and reloads are tracked here. Buy weapons in Gear → Market first.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: The dots are your actions this round: every button you press spends one. At the table the GM runs the rounds and the strip shows whose turn it is — your tablet chimes softly when it's yours.

steps.title: Hostiles
steps.text: The enemies the GM has revealed, by letter, with a rough wound band and what you can see on them. Say “I shoot B” — the GM uses the same letters.

steps.title: Attacking: the roll window
steps.text: Attack opens the roll window. First the d20 to hit. On a hit it goes step by step: damage, then (Scavenger) Exploit, then where it lands for a ⌖ location attack. At every step press Roll, or type what your own dice show and press Enter. The total comes at the end. In the dark, a Light row suggests the right modifier — you confirm it.

steps.title: Your class engine
steps.text: Your class resource and your equipped abilities (up to 3). An ability turns green when you can use it now; otherwise the sheet tells you what's missing. The Class tour button explains your class in a minute.

steps.title: Checks: the roll window
steps.text: Tap a skill (or an attribute) to roll it: d20, equal or under the TN succeeds. The window shows the GM's difficulty — including Favourable, Easy and Very easy when someone helps you or things go your way — the tools you carry, the items in play (a hypo's +1, already counted) and, in the dark, Light. Locks: mechanical → Sleight of Hand, electronic → Electronics, networked → Hacking.

steps.title: Money and the Market
steps.text: Buy officially with your Credit Score (traced) or on the street with cash (untraced, marked up). Guns come with 2 spare magazines — more in the Ammo tab — and Reload uses one. Hackers need a deck and Scavengers an optic. Misc adds story items with no rules. Each inventory row has ⇄ to sell or give it to a player, and 🗑 to drop it. Items marked Story only have no dice effect: the GM rules on them.

steps.title: Your Dossier
steps.text: Identity, debt and backstory. At the table you can ask the GM to write or polish your backstory; the prompts for your own AI (story and portrait) are here too.

steps.title: Rules one tap away
steps.text: Any ⓘ opens a short rule with a link to the manual. Replay this tour any time from the ? button at the top of the sheet.

steps.title: Tactical Points
steps.text: TP start at 0 every fight. Every normal attack that hits gives +1 TP; Brace & Dig In gives +2, Steady Aim +1. No cap: bank them.

steps.title: Stance
steps.text: Defensive: ×0.5 damage dealt and taken. Attack: normal. Onslaught: ×1.5 dealt and taken. The sheet applies your stance to every damage roll.

steps.title: Finishers
steps.text: Abilities cost TP and move you between stances. Equip up to 3; green means ready now. Use rolls your Class TN and spends an action.

steps.title: Your deck
steps.text: The deck sets your RAM and heat cap. No deck, no hacks: buy one in Gear → Market → Decks, then pick it here. Mods add RAM or cooling.

steps.title: RAM and Heat
steps.text: Hacks need free RAM. Sustained hacks keep theirs locked until you release them (✕). Every hack adds heat, −1 each round. Heat at the cap = Blue Screen: sustained hacks crash and the deck is locked for a round.

steps.title: Hacks
steps.text: Each card shows its RAM and heat. Most hacks only touch cybernetic or synthetic targets — the Hostiles list shows which is which. Thermal Dump, Release Payload and Hard Reboot need no roll.

steps.title: Mend or Surge
steps.text: Every ability has two faces: Mend (support) and Surge (offense). Your mode picks which one fires. Switching is free, but Sync drops to 0.

steps.title: Field Sync
steps.text: Sync 0–3, Cold to Resonant: +1 for each ability used, +1 at round end if you held your mode. Losing HP costs 1. At Resonant you can fire both faces at once.

steps.title: Abilities
steps.text: Stronger abilities need a minimum Sync. Brownout moves take the rig offline until the end of next round. Keep your Tech Wizard behind cover.

steps.title: The Pendulum
steps.text: From −4 to +4. Cold (below 0): +2 TN on gun attacks. Hot (above 0): +1 damage and +1 square per move. The sheet applies both for you.

steps.title: Abilities swing it
steps.text: Each ability needs a side of the pendulum and shifts it when used. Wounded Smugglers drift +1 toward Hot at the end of each round.

steps.title: The rhythm
steps.text: Plan in Cold, take a hit, swing Hot, cash in with a reckless move, crash back to Cold. Desperate Gamble goes all-in.

steps.title: Your optic
steps.text: Range: how far away you can place Tells. Track: how many enemies hold your Tells at once. Buy one in Gear → Market → Optics; without one you have bare lenses (range 4, Track 1).

steps.title: Tells on enemies
steps.text: At the start of your turn place 1 Tell, or 2 if you're Unseen — full cover, or in the dark (switch In the dark on), and no attack last round. Max 3 per enemy. Tap an enemy to make it your target for abilities.

steps.title: Exploit
steps.text: When an attack hits, the roll window asks which enemy you hit and how many of its Tells to spend: +1d4 damage each, then they're gone. A miss spends nothing.

steps.title: Abilities
steps.text: They spend the target's Tells: 1 for a small edge, 2 for a big one, 3 for the finisher. Close Study and Case the Room place more Tells.

steps.title: The map on the table
steps.text: What your crew can see. Drag to look around, pinch or use the mouse wheel to zoom, Fit to see it all. Dark squares: never seen. Dimmed: seen before, nobody sees them now. Doors and windows let sight through; closed doors don't.

steps.title: Moving
steps.text: Drag your marker. Shaded squares are where you can reach; the line shows the route round walls. In combat, on your turn, one Move action gives you your squares for the round: step as you like, one square at a time if you want. This line tells you what you can do right now.

steps.title: Tap to check
steps.text: Tap a marker: line of sight (clear, cover likely, blocked), distance, and which of your weapons reach. Tap a piece to see what it is. Tap a door next to you to open or close it — in combat that's an Interact action; a locked one won't budge.

steps.title: Light and vision
steps.text: Your torch lights 4 squares for the whole crew — and shows the enemy where you are. Night-vision goggles see 6 squares in the dark; a thermal lens shows people as heat signatures, not the room; a flare (Use item) lights where it lands.

steps.title: Who's there
steps.text: You (filled), your crew, hostiles by letter, other people in purple. A dashed ring is a heat signature: someone in the dark that only thermal picks up.

steps.title: Fighting in the dark
steps.text: In the dark the roll window adds a Light row: a target you only see as heat −2, one you can't see −4; Stealth +2 unlit, −4 if you're lit or your torch is on; Perception −2 unless you have night vision or thermal. The sheet suggests, you confirm.
